10.1002_adfm.77228: Conventional atmospheric water harvesting technology is limited by air pollution, which threatens to contaminate the harvested water and undermine its safety. To address this challenge, we report a bifunctional, self‐cycled Fenton system that integrates airborne droplet capture with in situ purification for the direct production of clean water. The system is fabricated by a FeO X /ZnO(OVs)/Zn mesh, in which oxygen‐vacancy‐rich ZnO coupled with a Zn substrate continuously generates H 2 O 2 via electron transfer from the metallic Zn. The in situ produced H 2 O 2 is subsequently decomposed by the FeO X catalyst to yield highly reactive hydroxyl radicals (·OH), enabling simultaneous contaminant disinfection during fog collection. This self‐cycled design realizes continuous droplet harvesting and purification without external energy input (e.g., light or electricity), offering a self‐sustained strategy for atmospheric clean water harvesting. The system achieves nearly 99% removal of organic pollutants and a bacterial inhibition rate exceeding 99.99%. Furthermore, by incorporating the FeO X /ZnO(OVs)/Zn plate into a recirculation setup, we demonstrate its scalability for treating larger volumes of contaminated water. This work provides a sustainable, external‐energy‐free strategy to enhance water security in water‐stressed regions by addressing both water scarcity and safety challenges simultaneously.
10.1016_j.ejrh.2026.103576: Stormwater is one of the main sources of microplastics (MP) in the environment, and it is important to understand how MP dynamics vary with the different hydrological parameters involved during rainfall events. This study focuses on identifying key hydrological processes that partly explain inter- and intra- events variability of MP at the inlet point of a detention basin collecting stormwater from an industrial area. Five rainfall events were monitored over a one-year period to investigate the hydrological drivers of MP. The results indicate that the annual flux of MP per active surface brought into the detention basin by stormwater is 1.17 kg/year/ha and the total MP load represents 0.3% of the suspend solids load. The first flush phenomenon is debated in the study, since the results show that several events do not exhibit it. The abundance of MP does not seem to be significant at the beginning of the event. With regard to hydrological processes, a thorough investigation was carried out to highlight intra and inter events relationships. The results show that flow rate and turbidity are positively relied to MP contamination but also that cumulative intensity has a downward influence on MP contamination. This work provides new insights on the transfer of MP in stormwater and the hydrological processes that lead to intra and inter events variability of MP.
10.1016_j.gee.2026.03.016: Developing efficient systems for directional lignin depolymerization via cleaving the aryl ether bonds to produce high-value-added chemicals is intriguing but remains challenging. Herein, we report a crystal phase reconstruction strategy for the synthesis of heterogeneous Bi-(Et3N)0.3 catalyst with rich defect sites and high-valence Bi species, which exhibits promising performance towards the fluidized electrocatalytic hydrogenation (FECH) of lignin-derived 2-phenoxy-1-phenylethanol with full conversion and up to 60.7% yield of phenol formation. Experimental and theoretical results confirm that the high-valence Bi species is beneficial in promoting the rapid activation of the protons, while the rich-defect sites derived from the crystal phase reconstruction between Bi-O and Bi-N-C coordination optimize the adsorption-activation of oxygen-containing intermediates. Moreover, by manipulating the variation of current density, the dissociation efficiency of protons and the enrichment degree of the electron-rich ([PW10VIW2VO40]5−) groups of the phosphotungstic acid (HPW) electrolyte were modulated, enabling the controllable switching of the phenol generation pathway. This study elucidates that the synergy between defect sites and high-valence Bi metals could advance the rational design of efficient electrocatalytic systems for the directional and efficient cleavage of lignin Cꞵ-O-4 bonds for high-value-added chemicals.
